Morris was selected as the 41st pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and played the [[point guard]] position. He also played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the NBA as well as the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] and [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA D-League]]. He also played overseas in China, Russia and France. Morris spent two seasons playing [[college basketball]] with the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. While playing for the [[2010–11 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2010–11 team]], he was the [[Big Ten]] [[assist (basketball)|assists]] leader and set the Michigan single-season assist record (since broken by [[Trey Burke]]). He earned third team All-Big Ten honors his sophomore season. Prior to attending Michigan, Morris led [[Windward School]] to the 2009 California state championship while earning the [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) Division 5A State [[John R. Wooden Award#High School Player of the Year Award|John Wooden High School Player of the Year Award]]. He was a 2010–11 All-Big Ten 3rd team selection by the coaches and the media. The [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] named him as a 2nd team All-District selection for the district composed of Big Ten schools. ==Early life== Morris was raised in [[Carson, California]].{{cite web|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/nba/la-sp-darius-morris-20140911-story.html|title=Ex-Lakers pick Darius Morris, an L.A. product, seeks his NBA foothold|access-date=September 22, 2014|date=September 10, 2014|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|last=Cook, Everett}} In high school, Morris, the son of Dewayne Sr. and Robin Morris, attended [[Windward School]]. As a brash freshman, Morris promised the media that he would be able to dunk and lead Windward to a state championship before he graduated. ==High school career== Morris was invited to numerous All-star basketball camps hosted by [[LeBron James]], [[Steve Nash]], the [[National Basketball Players Association]] and [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]]. He was twice selected as a first-team All-State player in California. He was also named the MVP of numerous tournaments and invited to participate in numerous all-star games, including the Academic All-American Classic.{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110701033408/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/morris_darius00.html |archive-date=July 1, 2011 |url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/morris_darius00.html |title=4 Darius Morris |access-date=March 7, 2011 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |website=MGoBlue.com |url-status=dead }} Morris's father worked for the [[United States Postal Service]] office in [[Venice, Los Angeles|Venice]]. As a senior, Morris led Windward High School to the California Division V state title, posting a game-high 25 points, eight rebounds and four assists in the championship game.
